title: MarinOS application security.json
description: Schema for a deployed MarinOS application's security.json. Identity fields (app id, name, repo, owner) live in the app's own marin.yml, not here — see marin-os/security/README.md for why. Standard language and profile definitions live in marin-digital-standards/security/.

$schema.description: Instance documents reference this schema file (e.g. './schemas/security.schema.json' or the raw GitHub URL) so editors can validate/autocomplete against it.

$comment.description: Free-text documentation for whoever reads this file next (e.g. why a profile default was overridden). Not read by any generator/validator logic.

schema.description: Standard version this file conforms to, matching marin.yml's plain-integer schema field convention.

profile.description: See marin-digital-standards/security/profiles.md for what each profile requires.

contact.description: One or more contact URIs (mailto:, https:), per the security.txt spec.

expires.description: Required by the security.txt spec. generate-security-txt.js should refuse to emit an already-expired file.

status.description: 'inherited-from-platform' is the expected value for a github.io deployment — HSTS is very likely already in effect via github.io's HSTS preload status, not something the app configures itself. Confirm rather than assume; see standard.md.

headers.description: Controls that require a real HTTP response header. On GitHub Pages, these are not achievable by the application itself — see standard.md, 'What GitHub Pages can and can't do.' Use status 'not-achievable' rather than omitting the field or falsely marking it 'enabled'.

status.description: Clickjacking protection. Not achievable via meta-delivered CSP (frame-ancestors is ignored when CSP arrives via <meta>) and not achievable via X-Frame-Options on GitHub Pages. A known, standing gap on the current hosting stack unless a documented exception says otherwise. Use 'not-applicable' (not 'not-achievable') when there's no rendered page to clickjack in the first place, e.g. a pure data API.

deliveryMechanism.description: 'header' is not currently possible on GitHub Pages; record 'meta' honestly rather than aspirationally.

directives.description: Directive name to list of sources. Baseline + app-specific additions combine per standard.md — this field holds the app's effective policy, not just its additions.

frame-ancestors.description: Ignored by browsers when CSP is delivered via <meta> (deliveryMechanism: meta). Recording it here is documentation of intent, not a claim that it's enforced.

notes.description: Plain-language context only. Never provider secrets, client IDs, or endpoint configuration here.

serverSideEnforced.description: false is the honest answer for a purely static, client-side MarinOS app — there is no server in the request path to enforce anything. See standard.md.

runtimeCdnPolicy.description: Expected value references marin-digital-standards/product-design/runtime-dependencies.md rather than restating it.

monitoring.description: Records GitHub Advanced Security org-level status. Does not duplicate it with app-level scanning tooling.

publicSecurity.description: The only part of this file a public #security section may render. Never generate #security from the full document.

controls.description: High-level control names only (e.g. 'HTTPS', 'Content Security Policy') — never directive-level CSP detail or anything from headers/csp/exceptions verbatim.

data.description: Factual, public-safe subset of the data{} block above.

githubNativeControl.description: Records GitHub's own org-level Advanced Security status rather than a custom implementation.
